name: Crypto value-at-risk sort, faithful port of the stock rule: 5% daily loss over 365 days, top third, monthly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0, {} = cash; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. Eligible = symbols with L >= need; n = |eligible|; if n < minNames return ew. VaR_s = -(the kth lowest of ret(b,e-j), j = 0..window-1) with k = ceil(q*window) (empirical quantile, no interpolation). Hold the floor(n/3) highest VaR_s (6 when n = 18), equal weight, ties by name ascending. Monthly, long-only. (Same as c1031-r4-01 except window 365, k = 19, monthly: the stock rule's one-year window and monthly cadence.)
rationale: Idea 1 states 180 days weekly; the stock survivor used a one-year window monthly. Running the faithful port as well separates 'VaR works in crypto' from 'VaR works at this lookback and cadence'.
source: campaign-1024/REPORT.md section 4 idea 1 (variant: the acad3-05 horizon and cadence); Bali & Cakici 2004 JFQA (window-informed: the idea comes from the round-3 forward summary, so it is reported, never CONFIRMED)

name: Crypto intersection of the bottom half by BTC correlation and the top half by 180-day value-at-risk, monthly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0, {} = cash; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. Eligible = symbols with L >= need; n = |eligible|; if n < minNames or BTCUSDT has L < need return ew. corr_s = Pearson correlation of ret(b_s,k) and ret(b_BTC,k) over k = e-corrWindow+1..e (BTCUSDT gets corr = 1). VaR_s = -(the 9th lowest of ret(b,e-j), j = 0..179). Lo = the ceil(n/2) lowest corr_s; Hv = the ceil(n/2) highest VaR_s (ties by name ascending). I = Lo intersect Hv. If |I| >= minHold hold I at 1/|I| each; otherwise hold Lo at 1/|Lo| each. Monthly, long-only.
rationale: If the tail-loss sort and the low-BTC-correlation sort are one factor, intersecting them should not beat either; if they are different the intersection is the cleaner version, as the momentum x downside-beta intersection was in US stocks.
source: campaign-1024/REPORT.md section 4 idea 1 (the one-factor test); extends c1024-acad3-05 and c1024-r3-02; intersection construction of c1024-r3-11 and c1022-redteam-07 (window-informed: the idea comes from the round-3 forward summary, so it is reported, never CONFIRMED)

name: Low BTC-correlation sleeve with hold buffer and inverse-volatility sizing on the 14 frozen pre-2020 discovery coins, monthly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0, {} = cash; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. corr_s = Pearson correlation of ret(b_s,k) and ret(b_BTC,k) over k = e-window+1..e (BTCUSDT gets corr = 1); a symbol with L < need is skipped; if BTCUSDT has L < need return ew; n = number of scored symbols; if n < minNames return ew. Rank ascending by corr; percentile p_s = (position-1)/(n-1). Hold set H in ctx.state (starts empty; ctx.state.H === undefined -> []): drop s from H if it is unscored or p_s > holdPct; then add symbols in ascending corr order (skipping ones already in H) until |H| = ceil(selectPct*n) (exactly c1023-r2-05's buffer). sigma_s = sample standard deviation of ret(b_s,k) over k = e-window+1..e. w_s = (1/sigma_s) / sum over H of (1/sigma); weights sum to 1. If n < minNames or BTCUSDT has L < need: reset H to empty and return ew. Monthly, long-only. Identical to c1024-r3-02 in every parameter; the only change is that the view is the 14 frozen coins (so n <= 14, target = ceil(0.5*n) <= 7).
rationale: r3-02 is the best-behaved A construction and r3-03 is the survivorship control, but only for the plain equal-weight rule. This runs the stronger construction on the same frozen list, one spec, so the survivorship control applies to the version people would use.
source: campaign-1024/REPORT.md section 4 idea 2; extends c1024-r3-02 and c1024-r3-03 (frozen list); Novy-Marx & Velikov 2016 RFS; Asness, Frazzini & Pedersen 2012 FAJ (window-informed: the idea comes from the round-3 forward summary, so it is reported, never CONFIRMED)

name: Low correlation to the equal-weight alt index excluding BTC (leave-one-out), bottom half, 70th-percentile hold buffer, inverse-vol sizing, monthly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0, {} = cash; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. Eligible = symbols with L >= need; n = |eligible|; if n < minNames or fewer than 4 non-BTC eligible symbols return ew. For symbol s, the reference return on bar k is a_s,k = mean of ret(b_s',k) over eligible s' with s' != BTCUSDT and s' != s (BTCUSDT is never in the index; the symbol is never in its own index, so BTCUSDT is scored against the mean of all eligible alts). corr_s = Pearson correlation of ret(b_s,k) and a_s,k over k = e-window+1..e. Then c1024-r3-02's rule unchanged: rank ascending by corr_s; percentile p_s = (position-1)/(n-1); hold set H in ctx.state (undefined -> []): drop s from H if it is unscored or p_s > holdPct; add symbols in ascending corr order (skipping ones in H) until |H| = ceil(selectPct*n); sigma_s = sample std of ret(b_s,k) over the window; w_s = (1/sigma_s)/sum over H of (1/sigma); weights sum to 1. If n < minNames reset H to empty and return ew. Monthly, long-only.
rationale: Round 2's low-BTC-beta and low-correlation sorts survived while a sort against the whole crypto index (redteam-03, beta) was a different construction. Measuring correlation against the alt index with BTC removed asks whether 'least tied to BTC' or 'least tied to the alt market' is the thing.
source: campaign-1024/REPORT.md section 4 idea 4; extends c1024-r3-02 (reference changed from BTC to the EW alt index), contrast c1022-redteam-03 (window-informed: the idea comes from the round-3 forward summary, so it is reported, never CONFIRMED)

name: r3-02 low-correlation sleeve in greed and neutral, cash in fear (Fear & Greed <= 40), monthly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0, {} = cash; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. corr_s = Pearson correlation of ret(b_s,k) and ret(b_BTC,k) over k = e-window+1..e (BTCUSDT gets corr = 1); a symbol with L < need is skipped; if BTCUSDT has L < need return ew; n = number of scored symbols; if n < minNames return ew. Rank ascending by corr; percentile p_s = (position-1)/(n-1). Hold set H in ctx.state (starts empty; ctx.state.H === undefined -> []): drop s from H if it is unscored or p_s > holdPct; then add symbols in ascending corr order (skipping ones already in H) until |H| = ceil(selectPct*n) (exactly c1023-r2-05's buffer). sigma_s = sample standard deviation of ret(b_s,k) over k = e-window+1..e. w_s = (1/sigma_s) / sum over H of (1/sigma); weights sum to 1. Gate added after the weights are built: g = ctx.macro('FNG') read at the rebalance-day close; if g is not null and g <= fear return {} (cash for the month); otherwise (greed, neutral or null) return the sleeve weights. rationale: The one regime gate that survived the battery in round 3 was a Fear & Greed cash leg on a momentum rule; the low-correlation sleeve is the tilt that held three times. This applies the gate to the standing tilt.

name: r3-02 low-correlation sleeve refreshed monthly but gated weekly: cash whenever Fear & Greed <= 40 at a weekly decision
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0, {} = cash; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. Weekly rebalance. State: ctx.state.M (UTC calendar month of the last refresh, undefined at start), ctx.state.W (frozen weights), ctx.state.H (hold set). month(t) = the UTC calendar month (year*12+month index) of the last bar of BTCUSDT in the view. If month(t) != ctx.state.M (first weekly decision of a month, or the first call): run c1024-r3-02's step exactly (corr to BTC over 90 days, hold buffer via H, inverse-vol weights, ew + reset of H if n < minNames or BTCUSDT has L < need), store the resulting weights in ctx.state.W and set ctx.state.M = month(t). Every weekly decision: g = ctx.macro('FNG'); if g is not null and g <= fear return {}; otherwise return ctx.state.W. Long-only.
rationale: A monthly refresh with a monthly gate can sit in the sleeve for three weeks of a fear regime. This keeps the sleeve construction monthly (same turnover as r3-02) and lets only the cash gate act weekly, as r3-07 does, isolating the cadence of the gate from the cadence of the sleeve.
source: campaign-1024/REPORT.md section 4 idea 5 (gate cadence variant); extends c1024-r3-02 and c1024-r3-07 (window-informed: the idea comes from the round-3 forward summary, so it is reported, never CONFIRMED)

name: r3-07 with Fear & Greed thresholds 50/30 (-10) and a one-week hysteresis on regime flips, weekly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0, {} = cash; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. g = ctx.macro('FNG') (null before 2018-02); thresholds greed = 50, fear = 30. Hysteresis (one week): raw_t = GREED if g is not null and g >= greed, FEAR if g is not null and g <= fear, else NEUTRAL (g null -> NEUTRAL). State in ctx.state: eff (effective regime, undefined at start) and prev (previous weekly raw regime). First call: eff = raw_t, prev = raw_t. Later calls: if raw_t != eff and prev == raw_t (the new regime held at two consecutive weekly decisions) then eff = raw_t; otherwise eff unchanged; then prev = raw_t. Weights by eff: GREED -> hold the top `top` eligible by score, 1/top each (1/|eligible| each if fewer); FEAR -> {} (cash); NEUTRAL -> equal weight over eligible. eligible = symbols with L >= lookback+1, score_s = b[e].close/b[e-lookback].close-1, ties by name ascending (c1024-r3-07's legs byte-for-byte). Weekly, long-only.
rationale: Thresholds moved 10 points toward fear (greed 50, fear 30) with the one-week hysteresis; r3-07's round-3 neighbours moved only the lookback, never the thresholds that define the gate.
source: campaign-1024/REPORT.md section 4 idea 6; extends c1024-r3-07 (thresholds are its fragile parameter; its neighbours only moved lookback) (window-informed: the idea comes from the round-3 forward summary, so it is reported, never CONFIRMED)

name: r3-07 with the greed leg replaced by the low-BTC-correlation sleeve: sleeve in greed, equal weight when neutral, cash in fear, weekly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0, {} = cash; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. g = ctx.macro('FNG') (null before 2018-02). If g is not null and g >= greed: return the sleeve. If g is not null and g <= fear: return {} (cash). Otherwise (neutral or null): equal weight over scored symbols (ew if BTCUSDT has L < need). Low-correlation sleeve: scored = symbols with L >= need (need = 92); n = |scored|; if BTCUSDT has L < need or n < minNames (8) return ew. corr_s = Pearson correlation of ret(b_s,k) and ret(b_BTC,k) over k = e-90+1..e (BTCUSDT gets corr = 1); sleeve = the ceil(n/2) lowest corr_s (ties by name ascending), equal weight, stateless (no hold buffer). Weekly, long-only. Neutral and fear legs are c1024-r3-07's unchanged; only the greed leg changes (two-week top-4 momentum -> sleeve).
rationale: Round 3 separated r3-07's two legs but not its two greed choices. Swapping the greed leg to the standing tilt separates 'cash in fear' from 'momentum in greed'.
source: campaign-1024/REPORT.md section 4 idea 7; extends c1024-r3-07 and c1023-r2-05/c1024-r3-02 (sleeve) (window-informed: the idea comes from the round-3 forward summary, so it is reported, never CONFIRMED)

name: Intersection of top-half value-at-risk and top-half downside beta, equal weight (wide US stocks), monthly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0, {} = cash; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. Downside beta (r25-downside-beta-high construction): elig = symbols with L >= need; M = |elig|; if M < minNames return ew; market m_j = mean over elig of ret(b,e-j), j = 0..252-1; down = {j: m_j < 0}; if |down| < 60 return ew; md = mean of m over down, var = sum over down of (m_j-md)^2 (if var <= 0 return ew); beta_s = sum over down of (r_s,j - rd_s)(m_j - md) / var with rd_s = mean of r_s over down (same centring as the parent module). VaR_s = -(the 13th lowest of the 250 daily returns ret(b,e-j), j = 0..249) on elig (5% empirical quantile, ceil(0.05*250) = 13, no interpolation, exactly c1024-acad3-05's measure). Hv = the ceil(M/2) highest VaR_s; Hb = the ceil(M/2) highest beta_s (ties by name ascending). I = Hv intersect Hb; if |I| < minHoldings (10) return ew; hold I at 1/|I| each. minNames = 50, need = 254. Monthly, long-only.
rationale: The two sorts that survived as the repeated US downside-risk results, built as the intersection construction that passed the exposure check in two earlier rounds rather than as a blend.
source: campaign-1024/REPORT.md section 4 idea 8; extends c1024-acad3-05, c1024-r3-11, c1024-r3-10 (r25-downside-beta-high) (window-informed: the idea comes from the round-3 forward summary, so it is reported, never CONFIRMED)

name: Value-at-risk top quintile with the sleeve volatility matched to the EW universe, residual in cash, exposure check (e) as a hard gate (wide US stocks), monthly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0, {} = cash; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. elig = symbols with L >= need (254); M = |elig|; if M < minNames return ew. VaR_s = -(the 13th lowest of the 250 daily returns ret(b,e-j), j = 0..249) on elig (5% empirical quantile, ceil(0.05*250) = 13, no interpolation, exactly c1024-acad3-05's measure). N = max(minHoldings, round(fraction*M)); sleeve = the N highest VaR_s (ties by name ascending). sigma_S = sample std over j = 0..volWindow-1 of (mean over sleeve of ret(b,e-j)); sigma_M = same for elig; w = sigma_S > 0 ? min(1, sigma_M/sigma_S) : 1. Weights: w/N on each sleeve name, residual 1-w in cash (identical construction to c1024-r3-09 and c1024-r3-15 applied to the VaR sort). Monthly, long-only. Gate (declared now, applied at retest, same wording as c1024-r3-09): this id counts as ahead only if the retest exposure check (e) passes (strategy CAGR > exposure x B&H CAGR and strategy Sharpe > B&H Sharpe); a check-(e) fail is a FAIL regardless of excess. Pre-registered expectation from r3-09/r3-15: zero edge.
rationale: The same falsification the downside-beta and momentum sorts got. If the VaR sort's edge is only the sleeve's higher volatility this lands near zero; if it does not, VaR differs from the beta sort.
source: campaign-1024/REPORT.md section 4 idea 11; extends c1024-acad3-05, c1024-r3-09, c1024-r3-15 (window-informed: the idea comes from the round-3 forward summary, so it is reported, never CONFIRMED)
prereg_note: Overseer: pre-registered expectation is zero edge (construction test); kept because the exposure gate (e) is the point.

name: Downside beta top quintile with a hold buffer (keep while within the top 40%), wide US stocks, monthly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0, {} = cash; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. minNames = 50, need = 254. Downside beta (r25-downside-beta-high construction): elig = symbols with L >= need; M = |elig|; if M < minNames return ew; market m_j = mean over elig of ret(b,e-j), j = 0..252-1; down = {j: m_j < 0}; if |down| < 60 return ew; md = mean of m over down, var = sum over down of (m_j-md)^2 (if var <= 0 return ew); beta_s = sum over down of (r_s,j - rd_s)(m_j - md) / var with rd_s = mean of r_s over down (same centring as the parent module). Score = beta_s. Rank all elig descending by the score (position 1 = highest); pos_s = that position. Hold set H in ctx.state (undefined -> []): drop s from H if it is not in elig or pos_s > ceil(holdFrac*M) (holdFrac = 0.4); then add names in descending score order (skipping ones already in H) until |H| = N, where N = max(minHoldings, round(fraction*M)), fraction = 0.2, minHoldings = 10. rationale: The hold buffer was the one change that reduced cost in the crypto sleeve and has never been given to the US downside-beta book, whose cost margin is only 2.4-2.8pp at doubled costs and whose cost is turnover.

name: Vol-scaled momentum among high-volatility, top-half dollar-volume names with the lookback decided by a 3/6/12-month vote (wide US stocks), monthly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0, {} = cash; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. elig = symbols with L > 260 (acad-61's guard); N = |elig|; if N < minNames return ew. dv_s = mean of close*volume over k = e-dvWindow+1..e; liquid = the ceil(N/2) highest dv (c1023-r2-16). vol_s = sample std of ret(b,e-m), m = 0..volBars-1, on liquid; HV = the floor(highVolFrac*|liquid|) highest-vol names within liquid. Momentum vote: for each horizon h in {63, 126, 252}: mom_h,s = b[e-21].close/b[e-h].close-1 (skip 21; 3-1, 6-1, 12-1 months). Let k = floor(topFrac*|liquid|). For each h, Top_h = the k highest mom_h,s within HV. votes_s = number of horizons h with s in Top_h. sleeve = the k names in HV with the most votes, ties broken by the highest mom_126,s (the tie horizon, fixed now) then name ascending (k < 3 -> return ew). Then c1024-r3-14 unchanged: spread series s_j = mean over sleeve of ret(b,e-j) - mean over elig of ret(b,e-j), j = 0..spreadWindow-1; sd = sample std of s * sqrt(252); w = sd > 0 ? min(1, target/sd) : 1. Weights: (1-w)/N on every elig name plus w/k on each sleeve name. Monthly, long-only.
rationale: A single momentum horizon is C's fragile parameter (three ids failed neighbours); the 3/6/12-month vote fixed the same weakness in the ETF switcher. This applies the vote to the one US momentum book that was already exposure-treated.

name: 9-ETF dual momentum with the SHY hurdle and the 20% volatility overlay together, remainder in the best bond, monthly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0, {} = cash; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. Risk-off: {bestBond: 1}; if no bond is scored hold ew. Monthly, long-only.
rationale: The two single changes with the lowest discovery p-values of round 3 (SHY hurdle, 20% volatility overlay) were never combined; this asks whether they stack.
